items.item_text: Any combination of training and experience which would provide the required knowledge, skills, and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the required qualifications would be e quivalent to an Associate’s degree from an accredited college with major coursework in photography or a related field AND three (3) years of experience working as a photographer or similar experience.
Experience supporting photography instruction in a college, university, community arts, commercial photography, or similar educational environment.
Experience with both digital and traditional photographic processes, including digital cameras, studio lighting, scanning, digital printing, enlargers, and traditional wet-darkroom processes.

Proficiency with Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Lightroom Classic, Capture One, and other post-processing software, with experience in digital imaging workflows, file preparation, post-production, and image archiving.

Experience operating and maintaining professional photographic printers and working with color-managed printing workflows, including monitor calibration, printer profiling, paper profiles, and preparation of exhibition-quality photographic prints.
Experience maintaining, troubleshooting, and performing routine repairs on photography, studio, printing, scanning, computer, darkroom, and related instructional equipment.
Experience supporting specialized photography laboratories, studios, traditional wet darkrooms, digital imaging labs, equipment checkout operations, and other technical instructional environments.

Experience with the safe handling, storage, use, and disposal of photographic chemistry and other hazardous materials associated with traditional wet-darkroom operations, including familiarity with applicable safety procedures and Safety Data Sheets (SDS).
Experience with gallery, museum, exhibition, or art-installation operations, including preparing, handling, installing, and deinstalling artwork.
Experience with gallery lighting, exhibition presentation, artwork labels and signage, framing or presentation systems, and maintaining professional exhibition spaces.
Experience supporting student, faculty, and visiting artist exhibitions, receptions, lectures, or other public-facing arts programming.
Experience managing equipment, supplies, inventories, purchasing, and/or equipment checkout systems.

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/. *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Principles and procedures for setting-up, operating, demonstrating use of, maintaining, and repairing various equipment used in photography programs.
Assist students and faculty and demonstrates proper use and maintenance of equipment, materials, and supplies used in photography programs.
